# Button group

Related buttons joined into one control.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Dense data</span></p>

## When to use it

**In Dense data:** A few toolbar actions that belong together, such as previous and next. Not for unrelated actions or a choice that stays pressed.

- **Use it when:** A few actions that belong together, such as previous and next, or a split action.
- **Not when:** A choice that stays selected (toggle group), or unrelated actions.

Instead:

- [Toggle group](./toggle-group.md): The choice stays pressed.
- [Dropdown menu](./dropdown-menu.md): More actions than fit in a row.

## Words

- Lead with the object, then the state: "Alert 2041 contained."
- Use numbers, not words for numbers.
- One verb per button. No "please", no exclamation marks.
- Use: Investigate, Filter, Assign, Escalated, Resolved. Avoid: Oops, Awesome, Please, Simply.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Delete
- `content.action.retry`: Retry
- `content.action.empty-action`: Change filters

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

Test before you ship:

- [ ] The buttons are a group with a name. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add button-group
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Tokens it reads

Button group reads 9 tokens of its own, each an alias of a semantic token. Each row is one part: its own token, the semantic it aliases, and the value it ends at. Change a semantic and every component that reads it follows; override one of Button group's tokens to change Button group alone.
